explanation.text:
(Pro. 22:1-29)

A good name-- (Job 30:8, Hebrew); "good" is supplied here from Ecc 7:1.

loving favour--kind regard, that is, of the wise and good.

bsb.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.

explanation.text: Before God all are on the same footing (Pro 14:31; Pro 17:5).

bsb.text: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.

explanation.text: are punished--that is, for their temerity; for the evil is not necessarily punitive, as the prudent might otherwise be its objects.

bsb.text: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.

explanation.text: humility and the fear of the Lord--are in apposition; one produces the other. On the results, compare Pro 3:16; Pro 8:18.

bsb.text: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.

explanation.text: he that . . . them--Those who properly watch over their own souls are thus preserved from the dangers which attend the way of perverse men (Pro 16:17).

bsb.text: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.

explanation.text:
Train--initiate, or early instruct.

the way--literally, "his way," that selected for him in which he should go; for early training secures habitual walking in it.

bsb.text: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

explanation.text: The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare Pro 19:6; Pro 21:14, etc.).

bsb.text: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:18; Psa 109:16-20; Gal 6:7-8).

the rod . . . fail--His power to do evil will be destroyed.

bsb.text: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

explanation.text:
a bountiful eye--that is, a beneficent disposition.

for he giveth . . . poor--His acts prove it.

bsb.text: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.

explanation.text: Cast out--or drive away. Scorners foster strife by taunts and revilings.

bsb.text: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.

explanation.text:
(Compare Margin).

pureness of heart--and gentle, kind words win favor, even from kings.

bsb.text: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.

explanation.text:
preserve--or guard.

knowledge--its principles and possessors.

overthroweth--utterly confounds and destroys the wicked.

bsb.text: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.

explanation.text: Frivolous excuses satisfy the indolent man's conscience.

bsb.text: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”

explanation.text: The mouth--or flattering speeches (Pro 5:3; Pro 7:5) ensnare man, as pits, beasts. God makes their own sin their punishment.

bsb.text: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.

explanation.text: is bound--or firmly fixed. Chastisement deters from crime and so leads to reformation of principle.

bsb.text: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

explanation.text: These two vices pertain to the same selfish feeling. Both are deservedly odious to God and incur punishment.

bsb.text: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.

explanation.text: Here begins another division of the book, marked by those encouragements to the pursuit of wisdom, which are found in the earlier chapters. It will be observed that at Pro. 22:22-24:12, the proverbs are generally expressed in two verses instead of one (see Introduction).

bsb.text: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise—apply your mind to my knowledge—

explanation.text:
These lessons must be laid up in the mind, and

fitted--or better, "fixed" in the lips so as to be ever ready.

bsb.text: for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.

explanation.text: That . . . Lord--This is the design of the instruction.

bsb.text: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today—yes, you.

explanation.text:
excellent things--or probably of former times.

counsels and knowledge--both advice and instruction.

bsb.text: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge,

explanation.text: Specially he desires to secure accuracy, so that his pupil may teach others.

bsb.text: to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you?

explanation.text:
Here follow ten precepts of two verses each. Though men fail to defend the poor, God will (Pro 17:5; Psa 12:5).

in the gate--place of public gathering (Job 5:4; Psa 69:12).

bsb.text: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,

explanation.text:
For the Lord will plead their cause,.... If counsellors at the bar will not, he will; if judges on the bench will not do them justice, he will; he will judge the poor of the people; he will plead their cause, and plead it thoroughly, till he has brought forth judgment unto victory: woe to the man against whom Jehovah pleads; happy the poor on whose side he is; for their Redeemer is mighty, the Lord of hosts is his name, Psalm 72:4;

and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them; they could only spoil the poor of their goods, but the Lord can and will spoil and destroy the souls of the spoilers in hell: or, "spoil them that spoiled their soul" or "life"; that is, who spoiled them of their goods, and took away that small pittance they had, which was their life or livelihood; they shall be spoiled themselves that spoil others; the same measure they have meted out shall be measured out to them again; God will destroy them that destroy the earth, even antichrist and his followers, the oppressors of Christ's poor on earth, Revelation 11:18.

bsb.text: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 2:12-15; Pro 4:14).

bsb.text: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,

explanation.text: a snare . . . soul--The unsuspecting are often misled by bad company.

bsb.text: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 6:1; Pro 17:18).

bsb.text: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.

explanation.text: should he take, etc.--that is, the creditor.

bsb.text: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 23:10). Do not entrench on others (Deu 19:14; Deu 27:17).

bsb.text: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.

explanation.text:
Success rewards diligence (Pro 10:4; Pro 21:5).

bsb.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
